blockers: Need clear contract for overload errors (429 vs 503) + Retry-After semantics across chat + embeddings routes

notes:
Account summary
- Banyan Search is a mid-market customer with spiky, event-driven traffic (product launches + weekly batch re-indexing) and large variance in prompt length (long context retrieval payloads). Primary workloads: chat completions (streaming) + embeddings + reranking.
- They are sensitive to tail latency and timeouts because their frontend is synchronous and they fan out multiple requests per end-user query.

Current usage + pain points (from calls + tickets)
- Pattern: stable baseline during business hours, then sharp bursts (5–10x) during campaigns. During bursts they saw p95 climb from ~1.6–2.2s to 10–25s, plus occasional client-side timeouts.
- They run aggressive retries in their app layer today (3 retries w/ short backoff). This helped with transient network blips but made overload situations worse ("it turns into a thundering herd"). They asked for canonical Retry-After guidance and whether Redwood errors are safe to retry.
- Noisy-neighbor concern: they want assurance their high-variance jobs won’t degrade other tenants and that they won’t be penalized by other tenants’ bursts.

Incidents / support history
- SUP-2841 (Jan): intermittent 503s on /v1/chat/completions in us-east during peak. Customer reported long streams getting cut off; logs show correlation IDs with elevated gateway timeouts.
- SUP-2860 (Feb): noticed some overload responses missing Retry-After header on specific routes; they were unable to implement consistent backoff until fixed.
- SUP-2892 (Feb): configured fallback (model variant + secondary region) but did not observe fallback triggering during a burst; they suspect loop-prevention / policy evaluation mismatch. They asked for a way to confirm fallback attempts (even if not taken) via response metadata or dashboard.

Requirements (explicit)
- Clear semantics for overload: prefer 429 when they are above tenant limits; 503 when platform is saturated; error payload must include stable error code + correlation_id.
- Retry contract: must include Retry-After (seconds) and guidance about when to retry vs when to fail fast.
- Fallback routing: want ability to configure (a) compatible model variant fallback under overload and (b) regional fallback (us-west) if us-east is constrained, with guardrails and no silent quality regressions.
- Graceful degradation interest: willing to accept caps on max_tokens and reduced streaming concurrency during overload if it prevents timeouts.

Commercial / packaging
- Exploring moving bursty workloads to Dedicated for predictable throughput, while keeping long-tail small tenants on Hosted API. They asked for a "burst buffer" option (reserved baseline + limited overflow) and how policy-based shedding would work per tier.

Internal notes / actions
- Shared draft guidance on overload errors + recommended client strategy (respect Retry-After; exponential backoff + jitter; stop retries after N; treat 4xx vs 5xx differently). Ibrahim to send code snippet for Python + TS.
- SRE context: this account is a good early signal for Hosted overload protection rollout effectiveness; watch shed-rate metrics vs reported timeouts.
- Routing follow-up: Mina/Ravi team to verify their tenant policy for fallback model + region and confirm loop-prevention config; propose adding lightweight debug header for enterprise tenants (e.g., X-Redwood-Fallback-Attempted: true) if allowed.

Next customer touchpoints
- 2026-02-26: technical review focusing on (1) overload error taxonomy, (2) retry/backoff, (3) fallback routing behavior, (4) Dedicated sizing.
- Banyan to provide: last 14 days of request counts by route/model, prompt length distribution, and peak concurrency window (they said they can export from their internal gateway logs).

Quotes (verbatim-ish)
- "We can live with being told ‘try again in 2 seconds’, but we can’t live with hanging requests that just die."
- "If you give us a deterministic 429/503 and a Retry-After, we can make the UI degrade gracefully."
- "Fallback is great but only if it’s predictable — no mystery model swaps without us opting in."
